lines.text: You change one lint rule, and now two hundred files need fixing. A perfect job for an agent.
But every single edit asks for approval first. Allow, allow, allow, allow.
Two hundred identical approvals. You will say yes every time, so each click tells you nothing at all.
So you turn on YOLO mode, for just this task. Tool calls are approved automatically from now on.
You can set it on one task, or on a whole workspace of low risk work, like a docs site.
The agent sweeps through every file and nobody waits on you. Edit after edit, all auto approved.
So you can go for coffee, or work on something else. The agent does not need you for this one.
Every call is still written to the task history. Nothing is hidden, and you can inspect any edit afterward.
The sweep finishes, and lint comes back clean. You review the diff once, instead of approving it two hundred times.
The review happens where it should, in the diff, with the whole change in front of you.
And when the sweep is over, you switch it off, and the careful defaults come right back.
Two hundred clicks, down to zero. Try YOLO mode at Agent R Q dot com.
